# ACC002 `atomic-in-compute-region`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

An `!$acc atomic` inside an OpenACC compute region or device routine.

## Why

Atomics serialise the threads that hit the same address and are a frequent sign of a
parallelisation that does not match the data flow (a scatter where a gather would do, a missing
reduction). They are correct, but on a GPU they can cost more than the whole kernel. Treat each one
as a red flag: restructure as a gather or a `reduction` clause when possible, keep it only where
the scatter is inherent.

## Reported

```fortran
!$acc parallel loop
do e = 1, nedges
  !$acc atomic update
  flux(node(e)) = flux(node(e)) + f(e)
end do
```

## Preferred

```fortran
!$acc parallel loop
do n = 1, nnodes            ! gather over the edges of each node
  flux(n) = sum(f(edges_of(:, n)))
end do
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[ACC002] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = ACC002` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/fobos/lint).
